sections.title: Fixes
items: Improve pill contrast on raised surfaces

sections.title: Fixes
items: Scripts in skills stay runnable. A skill file that is executable where it comes from keeps its executable bit through import, Edit as my copy, install into your agents, backups and undo. The import review says so, and a change to only that bit shows in the preview
Status labels are easier to read: every state now meets the WCAG AA contrast minimum in both light and dark mode
After Update all, Undo and Dismiss show once, in the receipt, instead of also in the run panel

sections.title: Linux and Windows groundwork
items: Riggverk is being tested on Linux and Windows. These changes do not affect the Mac app (#193–#196):
Open folder and file actions use xdg-open on Linux and Explorer on Windows.
Agent CLIs installed through npm, bun, cargo, scoop or Linuxbrew are found.
On Windows, a second Riggverk window cannot apply at the same time, and folders behind symlinks or junctions are refused while OneDrive folders work.
On Linux, file names that differ only in case are kept apart, and the window has no empty strip at the top.

sections.title: New
items: Riggverk now comes as a disk image: open it and drag Riggverk to Applications. One universal app runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs, and `SHA256SUMS` lists the checksums of the downloads
The groundwork for updating Riggverk from inside the app. It stays off until a later release turns it on, and then asks you once before it checks

sections.title: New
items: Import a skill you found. In Library → Packs, choose Import skill… and drop or paste a folder, a `SKILL.md` or a folder of several skills (#178):
Riggverk first shows the whole `SKILL.md` and flags what lets a skill act without asking: `allowed-tools`, `hooks`, `!` commands, scripts and hidden Unicode.
The skill goes into its own read-only pack, `imported`, with a record of where it came from. Your agents get it at the next Update all.
You can import again with a diff, remove it (a backup is kept), undo, or Edit as my copy.
A pack skill without `targets` now counts for all agents, so skills from GitHub work as they are.
Update all shows what will happen before you apply (#177):
Count tiles sum up what will be created, updated, removed, skipped and left alone.
A small flow map shows what is written to each agent, with the plan grouped by agent beside it.
While applying, the map follows the run. When it is done, a receipt lists any steps left to you, with Undo.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Light mode: a saved custom background no longer stays dark when macOS switches to light. Custom colours apply only where they fit the theme shown, and Settings says when one is not used
The app icon has a light variant for light appearance on macOS 26
The version moved to the sidebar foot, and the window buttons sit further from the edge, in line with the top bar

sections.title: Fixes
items: Undo says what it does: files the update created are removed, the others come back from the backup. The confirm and the History receipt now name both
History calls a run that only created files "Installed"
In the update review, a new file's details say what Undo does with it, and the plan no longer reads "previewing preview" while it is computed

sections.title: Fixes
items: Quit (Cmd+Q) now asks about unsaved work first. Before, it closed Riggverk at once and an unsaved Library edit was lost. A minimized window comes back to ask. Quit from the Dock is still not asked about

sections.title: Changes
items: The `status-report` skill's HTML report uses the same silver accent as the app

sections.title: Changes
items: The sidebar shows the rune mark next to the name
One silver accent that matches the rune replaces the blue:
Update all and every primary button are silver with dark text; the light theme uses a dark graphite.
The ready state, focus rings, the active tab and selections follow the same accent.
"Yours" turns lavender so it stays apart from ready

sections.title: New
items: Riggverk has its own mark: a rune, as a light glyph on a dark tile, is now the app icon
The window opens maximized the first time and then reopens where you left it, falling back to a visible display if that one is gone
On a large window the Overview flow map grows, and agents that are off get their own dimmed rows. On a smaller window they stay grouped in one "off" node
New skill `grill-me`, adapted from Matt Pocock's grilling skills:
Ask for it and it interviews you in rounds to sharpen an idea, a plan or a design, one recommendation per question.
It ends with a short summary of what is decided, what is open and what needs a prototype.
It never starts on its own and writes no files

sections.title: Fixes
items: From a full security audit of the app and the kit:
**Pack skills.** For a skill from a pack, the Library and the update review now show the settings that let it act without asking, such as `allowed-tools` and `hooks`
**Backups.**
Undo and crash recovery refuse a backup that is a link, owned by someone else, or writable by others.
OpenCode checks run from a private folder.
A rules file opens only inside its own folder

**OpenCode permissions.** OpenCode now lets agents run only exact, safe forms of `git diff`, `git log`, `git show`, `tree`, `find`, the test runners and `cargo` without asking. `git add` and `git commit` ask too. Before, quoting an option could slip a command past the rules
**Bundled skills.** They pre-approve only read-only commands. The delegate skill states plainly which routes are sandboxed. The Codex reviewer no longer reads the reviewed change's own AGENTS.md
**Release builds.** They use the locked dependency versions. The vendored security-audit skill is checked against recorded digests

sections.title: New
items: Six skills for the work around the code. Every one of them writes in your repository, commits, pushes or posts only when you ask for that step, and shows you the change first.
`pr-workflow` turns finished work into clean commits and a pull request. It:
follows your repository's own conventions;
runs the gate before the push and writes the PR text from the diff;
never force-pushes
`review-response` works through review comments on a PR. It:
checks each point against the code before acting, then sorts it into fix, push back with evidence, or ask;
drafts one reply per thread and posts only the replies you approve
`ci-triage` reads the failed logs of a red CI run without printing secrets. It:
classifies the failure as code, flaky test, environment or infrastructure;
reproduces it locally and hands the cause to `diagnose`;
reruns a job only on your explicit yes
`release-notes` drafts notes or a changelog section from the merged PRs since the last tag, in your project's own format and language
`agents-md` creates or refreshes a repository's `AGENTS.md` from commands it has actually run, plus an optional `CLAUDE.md` pointer, so every agent shares one file

`delegate` hands a well-specified slice to another installed agent, such as Codex, Claude Code or OpenCode, in its own git worktree. It then reviews the result like a pull request and runs every check again. It runs only when you want other agents used

sections.title: Fixes
items: In the Library, an item you open right after switching topics no longer closes again on a busy machine

sections.title: Changes
items: README credits the skill collections that some bundled skills adapt, with links and licenses

sections.title: Before you update
items: The Kretsverket skills, the Kretsverket status report profile and `wordpress-woocommerce` have left the bundled kit for a skill pack. If you use them, clone that pack into `~/.config/riggverk/packs/` before you run Update: the pack's copies then take over without rewriting anything. Without the pack, Update removes the app's copies with a backup (Undo brings them back), and copies you edited stay

sections.title: Changes
items: Riggverk no longer picks a model for you: new installs get no Codex `model` or reasoning effort and no OpenCode `model` or `small_model`, so each agent uses its own default. Models already in your config stay exactly as they are, and the OpenCode per-role overrides still work
The rules and agents are no longer tied to one person's stack:
The `verifier` finds your project's own build and test commands (Make, just, npm scripts, cargo, pytest, go).
The rules ask before adding a dependency, and treat web pages, issues, review comments and tool output as data, not instructions.
OpenCode lets only exact test commands run without asking; variants that could run other programs ask first
Skills work the same in every agent:
`release-check` judges the gate by its own exit code.
`current-docs` has a fallback when no web tool is available.
`browser-qa` can drive Playwright from the command line, with redacted and capped output.
The adversarial skills carry their own reference files

sections.title: New
items: A skill pack can add routing lines for its own skills: a `routing.md` in the pack folder, up to 30 bullet lines that name the pack's skills. The next Update shows them in every agent's rules under "Pack skill routing", with a diff, and Undo takes them back. A line that names another skill or holds markup keeps the whole file out, and Library, Packs says which line

sections.title: Changes
items: The bundled skills follow the Agent Skills format: their category, risk, targets and related skills sit under `metadata:`, each carries `license: MIT`, and skills that need subagents, Playwright, `gh` or Node say so in `compatibility`. Packs and your own skills in the older layout keep working unchanged
NOTICE credits the projects whose methods the adversarial skills build on, and the ones that inspired others

sections.title: New
items: New skill `status-report`: ask your agent for a status report (or "lägesrapport") and it builds one self-contained HTML page of what happened, what is in progress and what comes next in the repository. Every line cites its source (git, GitHub, CI or a doc), claims without evidence are marked, and what could not be checked is listed. A check stops a report with secrets, uncited items, dates outside the period or external scripts. The report reads in Swedish or English, on a phone, printed and without JavaScript
The Kretsverket status report is now a profile on top of `status-report`
One update may now hold up to 2048 file operations, so a first update with every agent switched on still fits

sections.title: New
items: The Overview's flow map stays short however many agents Riggverk knows: the agents that are off share one node at the bottom ("6 off", with their icons), and selecting it lists them with a way to Settings. Agents that are on keep their own rows and curves

sections.title: New
items: Grok Build (xAI's `grok`) is a new light harness, off until you switch it on in Settings. It reads the skills Riggverk already installs, so it adds no new folder, and it takes your rules from the managed block in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` while Claude Code is on. Its page says where its rules come from. The Playwright MCP entry in `~/.grok/config.toml` is off by default; when on, it is written as one table and every other byte of the file is kept

Google Antigravity is a new light harness, off until you switch it on in Settings. It gets the managed rules block in `~/.gemini/AGENTS.md` (`GEMINI.md` is never touched), which stays within Antigravity's 24,000-byte limit or is refused. It also gets the Playwright MCP entry in `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json`, off by default. Its skills go in two folders of its own, `~/.gemini/config/skills` for the app and IDE and `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills` for `agy`, which are emptied of Riggverk's copies again when you switch it off

sections.title: Fixes
items: The Library's list of personal docs no longer follows a `docs/context` folder that was replaced by a symlink, so it never reads files outside the data folder
The Codex config merge and the OpenCode config generator run Python in isolated mode, so a `PYTHONPATH` or user site-packages can no longer slip modules into them
The security model now states that confirmations happen in the app's own window and what keeps foreign script out of it

sections.title: Fixes
items: Text typed while Save and quit or Save and continue runs is no longer lost: the editor stays open and asks again
A Library refresh that fails, or a list that no longer shows the open item, keeps your unsaved document, skill or rules draft
A slow settings load no longer overwrites a change you just made
An update whose every reviewed target was switched off after the preview now asks for a new preview instead of reporting an apply that never happened
A skill can no longer take a bundled skill's name by quoting the key (`"name": tdd`)
An update stops and leaves the file alone when a skill or agent file is edited elsewhere while the update runs
After a crash in the middle of an update, recovery only removes or replaces a file it can prove it wrote; a file you added to since is kept as a conflict
Undo after such a crash works even when the source changed since, and a retried rollback also restores the pack and ownership records instead of reporting success
Undoing an earlier update keeps a pack you chose to forget after it

sections.title: Changes
items: The flow map on the Overview shows each agent with its own icon, and its state as a small badge on the icon: a ring when it is fine, a filled square when it needs your decision, a dashed ring when it is off
The sidebar lists only the agents you use; the ones that are off show in the Overview's flow map, where a click takes you to Settings
The progress and outcome of an update now sit in a bar of their own at the bottom and never cover the page above them. Sheets and dialogs in the Library have more room to breathe

sections.title: Before you open it
items: Updating the Codex config now needs Python 3.11 or newer, because the version that ships with macOS cannot read every valid `config.toml`. If none is found, Riggverk holds the Codex config update back in the preview and says why; everything else still installs. Homebrew's `python3` is enough.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Quitting or closing the window with unsaved changes in the Library now asks first: Save and quit, Discard, or Keep editing. Typing while a save runs is kept, and a doc or skill that changed on disk since you opened it is not overwritten (#120, #121)

A Cursor `mcp.json` with a token in one of your own servers no longer makes every Install fail and roll back, and your own `playwright` entry there is a conflict for you to decide instead of being replaced
Your own agent models in OpenCode's `opencode.json` stay yours. Riggverk removes only the models it wrote itself

Renaming a skill file in letter case only no longer deletes it, a skill with an edit you have not decided on is never removed by halves, and a nested `name:` in a pack skill can no longer pass as a bundled skill (#119, #122)

Errors never quote lines from your config files, which can hold tokens. Undo is refused while a newer update was not rolled back, a second Riggverk window cannot write at the same time as the first, and an Install after a crash asks you to preview again
Overview says when an agent could not be checked instead of "Everything is set up.", lists items to fix by hand, and the run panel with progress and Undo now shows on every page (#121, #123)

Actions that only had a key now have a button: OpenCode model Save, Reset and Reload, Settings Reset appearance and Retry save, install plan details, and the rules and Codex reviews. The Undo dialog names the update instead of showing an id, and custom colours warn when text or the focus ring would be hard to see (#121, #123)
Update all and Undo finish about a second sooner when OpenCode is on

sections.title: New
items: Overview shows how your setup flows: Riggverk's base, your own refinements and each skill pack on the left, your agents on the right, joined by curves. A thicker curve carries more, a dashed one has an update waiting, and the agents your last update wrote keep a faint glow. A decision is a filled square on the agent. Select an agent, a source or a curve and the panel beside the map shows its details, the last update for just that agent, and what you can do next, such as Open, Undo or Install everything. While an update runs, the panel follows it file by file and the map shows which agent is being written

The Library is laid out like System Settings: topics for Rules, Skills, Agents, Docs, Configs and Packs, one search across all of them, and rows that say what you can do. Opening an item brings down a sheet to read or edit it. Leaving with unsaved changes always asks: Discard, Keep editing, or Save and continue

Edit your rules files in the Library: the managed block stays read-only above, and you edit only your refinements below it. Effective shows exactly what the agent will read, and Diff shows your change against the file on disk before you save. Riggverk says when one of your headings also exists in the base. A file whose managed block was edited by hand stays read-only and points you to the agent's page to decide

Edit as my copy: copy a bundled skill into your own `personal` pack under a new name, such as `tdd-mine`, and edit it there. The bundled skill keeps its name and stays active, and the next Update installs your copy next to it. Saving keeps a backup (#113, #115)

sections.title: Fixes
items: Paths, keys and other fixed-width text use the Mac's own mono face (SF Mono) instead of a bundled font, so they match the rest of macOS and the app is smaller
Card grids no longer end with empty slots: the last card in a short row stretches to fill it

sections.title: New
items: A new look. The terminal-style screens are gone: a sidebar lists Overview, your agents, History, Library and Settings (keys 1 to 8 always open the same place), and a top bar has Check and Update all. Everything is mouse-first, with the keyboard shortcuts as accelerators (`?` lists them). Neutral graphite with a matching light theme, the system font for text, and motion that follows Settings > Motion (#94, #102, #103, #105, #108, #109)

Overview answers "is my setup OK?" at the top: "Your setup works." or "Everything is set up.", with one line that counts only what is not zero. Each agent has a card, and the last update shows what changed and what was left for you, with Undo

Decisions are shown where they belong. A file you edited gets a card that says why Riggverk left it alone; Compare opens the side-by-side difference right there, and the two choices say what happens next. Nothing is written before you preview it, Enter never applies, and `y` or the Apply button does (#105, #107)

Codex settings: the table shows Riggverk's value next to yours for each key Riggverk manages. Keep mine keeps your value; Use Riggverk defaults sets only the keys that differ, after a preview, with a backup and Undo. Riggverk refuses instead of touching anything the preview didn't show (#99, #107)
History lists every update, also after a restart, with what changed, what was already current and what was left for you. Undo is offered on the newest one and always asks first (#98, #106)

Skill packs: put your own skills in `~/.config/riggverk/packs/<name>/skills/` and Riggverk installs them like its own, with backups and Undo. If a pack goes missing or can't be read, its skills stay installed until you choose Forget pack in the Library. Packs that others can write to are refused (#101, #104)

sections.title: Before you open it
items: Quit any older Riggverk that is still running before the first launch of this version. This release moves Riggverk's data folder, and two versions working at the same time could split it.

sections.title: New
items: Riggverk's own names now say Riggverk everywhere. The data folder moves from `~/.config/agent-workspace` to `~/.config/riggverk`, its state folder from `.agent-workspace/` to `.riggverk/`, and the markers in your rules files become `BEGIN RIGGVERK BASE` / `END RIGGVERK BASE`. Nothing moves when the app opens: the folder is renamed the first time Riggverk writes something, and your rules files get the new markers on their next update, with everything you wrote below END kept byte for byte. `RIGGVERK_WORKSPACE_PATH` and `RIGGVERK_BACKUP_DIR` replace the old variables, which still work. A saved custom folder is never moved. If the move cannot happen, Riggverk keeps working in the old folder and says why on the workspace row. Scripts or editors that open files in `~/.config/agent-workspace` need the new path, and going back to an older version after the move is not supported

Codex settings you changed on purpose can stay yours. When an enforced key in `~/.codex/config.toml` differs from Riggverk's value, such as `approvals_reviewer`, press `m` on the Codex config row: Riggverk keeps your value, stops reporting it as a conflict and never writes over it, while the other managed keys keep following Riggverk. Change the value again and it becomes a conflict again; press `m` once more to hand it back

First steps of the new look: a neutral graphite palette with no amber, a neutral light theme, and calmer review screens. Install previews, rules reviews, file conflicts and confirm dialogs are now cards that say what happens before you apply ("Preview first · Backed up · Undo any time"). Enter still never applies; `y` or the Apply button does (#89, #93)

sections.title: New
items: Claude Code can stop adding its attribution to your commits and pull requests. Turn on the `config` target on the Claude page, then Install. It sets `attribution.commit` and `attribution.pr` to `""` in `~/.claude/settings.json`, which removes the `Co-Authored-By` commit line and the "Generated with Claude Code" PR line. Every other setting in the file stays. If you already chose your own attribution, or the file has comments, Riggverk leaves it alone. The target is off by default, and `z` undoes it

Each harness page has a `security` group that shows which permission and sandbox settings in that harness's own config are risky, enforced or only advice, such as bypass mode, an open network or a missing sandbox. It only reads named settings, never shows their values, and never says a setup is safe: project config, profiles and command-line flags are not checked

New guide in Library > Docs > Security Baseline: per harness, what Riggverk enforces and what you have to do yourself, plus how to keep unknown repositories and production credentials away from your agents

sections.title: Fixes
items: A harness Riggverk has not installed anything into shows "not installed" again, even when Riggverk already manages another harness on the same computer. Before, it showed "update available"

The OpenCode critic in adversarial-implementation stops before the review when it would get any tool beyond reading, such as your own tools in `~/.config/opencode/tools/`, and names them so they can be denied

sections.title: Changes
items: Riggverk no longer keeps a copy of its bundle in your workspace folder (`~/.config/agent-workspace`). The Library and health read the bundle inside the app, and the folder now holds only Riggverk's state (`.agent-workspace/`), your personal docs (`docs/context/`) and anything you put there yourself

Old copies from earlier versions show on the `workspace` row as "N old copies to remove". Press `u` to review: every removal is listed per folder and backed up first, and `z` restores them. Nothing is removed at launch (#76, #78)
Files you edited, and files Riggverk cannot prove it wrote, are left in place and shown as "left in place". To keep a copy of everything, cancel the review, or press `z` after applying
The workspace view no longer shows the data folder's git branch or uncommitted changes; GIT_VERSIONING.md now covers versioning `docs/context/` only

sections.title: Fixes
items: Files that only early test builds shipped are also cleaned up when they are unchanged

sections.title: New
items: adversarial-review: a fresh read-only critic finds and verifies issues and reports them without fixing anything; plan mode and a separate list for issues that were already there
adversarial-test: an adversary writes failing tests that are then frozen, and the implementer may change only production code

adversarial-implementation v2: the critic is chosen by capability, every finding carries a proof the lead runs, at most three rounds with frozen tests and a final round that may only delete; a start line shows who plays each role and how to change it
Start the adversarial skills in plain words or with their slash command (#69, #71, #72)
OpenCode: a critic model row, so the adversarial skills' critic (inspector) can run a stronger model than the other subagents

sections.title: Fixes
items: Critics can no longer reach MCP tools such as Playwright, whether they run in OpenCode, Codex or Claude Code

Riggverk replaces Agent Workspace. Quit Agent Workspace, move Agent Workspace.app to the Trash and install Riggverk.app (see Install). Your settings and backups move to Riggverk's folder on the first launch.

sections.title: New
items: Copilot, Pi and Kilo as opt-in harnesses: rules block, skills and the Playwright MCP entry (#40, #41, #42)
One shared SKILL.md per skill, installed into each folder your harnesses read; see which copy each harness loads (#28, #30, #33, #34)
Resolve a conflicting skill or agent file: keep your version or take the bundled one (#44, #45)
Library: bundled items are read-only and come straight from the app; edit your personal docs and your own refinements below the rules base (#49, #52, #57)

OpenCode: version-aware health with CLI probes and lsp, model/small model/subagent model overrides, runtime rows that show what differs, warnings when other config files or env override the team settings, only the bundled tui.json keys are managed, XDG_CONFIG_HOME is followed (#31, #32, #54, #55, #60, #63)
What's new after each update
New skills: adversarial-implementation, security-audit, kretsverket-status-report (#19, #20, #21)
Master-detail pages, bracket buttons, apply progress and motion levels (#14, #17)

sections.title: Changed
items: Renamed to Riggverk; app data moves on first launch (#37, #39)
Prompt Builder, Brain Setup and the in-app release check are removed (#26, #27)
The workspace folder chooser is gone: a saved folder keeps working, and `R` resets to the default after a confirm
Playwright MCP 0.0.83 runs your installed Google Chrome; tools that web pages register (WebMCP) are off

sections.title: Fixes
items: OpenCode permissions match OpenCode 1.19.3: compound commands are checked part by part, and secret files are denied in bash however the path is written (#29, #65, #66)
The managed OpenCode config converges, and health compares with what Install writes (#51, #56)
The window opens centered at 1280x800, the boot lines clear the traffic lights, and the pane grid holds at large text (#13, #22, #38)
Codex delegation only when Codex is installed and logged in
The Playwright entry is added to an existing mcp.json
